title: Darpan, a Telangana State Police tool, matches a boy missing from Allahabad to a child home in Assam, where his parents identify him after five years
summary: Darpan, a Telangana State Police facial-recognition tool, matched Som Soni, missing from Allahabad since 14 July 2015, to a boy in a child home in Goalpara, Assam, where his parents identified him.
account: Som Soni went missing from his home in Allahabad (Uttar Pradesh) on 14 July 2015, aged eight. ETV Bharat describes him as a resident of Handia in Allahabad, and the case lay with Handia police station. On 23 July 2015, Goalpara police found him and took him to a child welfare center at Goalpara, Assam (spelled “Golapara” in the reports). Darpan, a facial-recognition tool built by Telangana State Police, matches photographs of missing children against photographs of children lodged in child homes across the country. A routine matching run matched his photograph to the missing-child record from Uttar Pradesh. Telangana Police notified Handia police, and his parents traveled to Goalpara and identified him. Swati Lakra, Additional Director General of Police (ADGP) of the Telangana Police Women Safety Wing, announced the case on 9 October 2020. The reports do not give the exact day of the reunion. ANI reported on 12 October 2020 that Lakra had told it that Telangana State Police built Darpan in 2018. She said that the police draw data from child care institutions, the central Track the Missing Child portal and the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and System (CCTNS), and that Darpan had helped reunite about 33 children by then. In July 2023, Deccan Chronicle reported that Hyderabad police were still using Darpan and that it had helped reunite 36 children.
purpose: Darpan was built to match photographs of missing children with photographs of children found in institutions, so that the children can be returned to their families. This reunion is that intended benefit.
system: Darpan face-recognition portal for missing and found children
deployer: Telangana State Police, with Goalpara Police (Assam) and Handia Police Station (Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh)
domain: Policing / missing persons and child protection
taxonomy_note: The good is a family reunited, and the type names the identity match that located the boy.

ratings.reason: A child separated from his parents for five years, living in an institution in another state, was identified and returned to his family. The sources describe the match as having “changed the lives of the child and his parents”.

ai_role.statement: The face match was the sole lead. The boy had been in an Assam institution for five years with no identification until Darpan matched his photograph to the Uttar Pradesh missing-child record. Police then contacted the parents. Verification rested on the parents identifying him in person. The Telangana CID news page was not available. So the record relies on news reports quoting the ADGP.

fields.summary: Darpan, a Telangana State Police facial-recognition tool, matched Som Soni, missing from Allahabad since 14 July 2015, to a boy in a child home in Goalpara, Assam, where his parents identified him.
fields.account: Som Soni went missing from his home in Allahabad (Uttar Pradesh) on 14 July 2015, aged eight. ETV Bharat describes him as a resident of Handia in Allahabad, and the case lay with Handia police station. On 23 July 2015, Goalpara police found him and took him to a child welfare center at Goalpara, Assam (spelled “Golapara” in the reports). Darpan, a facial-recognition tool built by Telangana State Police, matches photographs of missing children against photographs of children lodged in child homes across the country. A routine matching run matched his photograph to the missing-child record from Uttar Pradesh. Telangana Police notified Handia police, and his parents traveled to Goalpara and identified him. Swati Lakra, Additional Director General of Police (ADGP) of the Telangana Police Women Safety Wing, announced the case on 9 October 2020. The reports do not give the exact day of the reunion. ANI reported on 12 October 2020 that Lakra had told it that Telangana State Police built Darpan in 2018. She said that the police draw data from child care institutions, the central Track the Missing Child portal and the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and System (CCTNS), and that Darpan had helped reunite about 33 children by then. In July 2023, Deccan Chronicle reported that Hyderabad police were still using Darpan and that it had helped reunite 36 children.

echoes.setting: Rahul Srivastava, missing from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh since 2010 (7 October 2010 per ETV Bharat; July 2010 per The Hans India), was matched by Darpan in March 2020 to a child welfare center in Howrah, West Bengal, and handed to his parents by West Bengal Police on 12 December 2020

Hyderabad: police used Darpan to find a girl from Kurnool who had been living in a children's home, and a second girl missing for two years (Deccan Chronicle, with its own interviews of the Anti Human Trafficking Unit inspector and a parent)
